text:
Marathon Petroleum stock ticked up 0.35% today to close at $363.54, continuing a modest recovery after a sharp dip on August 25th. The move appears tied to geopolitical tension around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran, which has kept crude prices elevated (US oil at $83.90/barrel, global at $88.24) and refineries running at 97.4% capacity—near maximum utilization. Tighter supply conditions and high refinery utilization typically support margins for refiners like Marathon.

The broader backdrop reinforces this: Middle East tensions are disrupting LNG flows to Europe and creating uncertainty around global energy supply, while U.S. refineries continue running hard. However, the news from August 27th also shows diplomatic de-escalation efforts underway, which could ease some of the geopolitical premium that's been supporting energy prices over the past few days.
